about.title: About Agent Atlas
about.body:
Agent Atlas is an educational project that helps to understand how AI agents work, communicate and are orchestrated.

## Educational use only

Agent Atlas is a learning tool. It is not meant for real work.

## Licences

- The code is open source under the MIT licence.
- The site text, articles and translations are under CC BY 4.0.
- The name and logo of Agent Atlas are not licensed for reuse.

## Source code

The code is open at [github.com/cimenta/agent-atlas-academy](https://github.com/cimenta/agent-atlas-academy).

## Bugs and ideas

Found a bug or have an idea? See [Bugs and ideas in Help](#/help/bugs).

## Legal

Read the [privacy policy](#/page/privacy), the [terms of use](#/page/terms) and the [imprint](#/page/imprint).

harness.title: Harness
harness.intro: The harness is everything around the model: the loop of agents, the limits, the time cap, retries and the rules for keys. The pages Limits, Retries, Fallback model, Cost, Guards and Tools hold what you can set, and Fixed harness the rules that always apply. Press ? next to a setting to read what it does.
harness.fallbackNote: The model it falls back to is fixed: Fast is replaced by Balanced, Balanced by Fast and Strong by Balanced, always within the same provider and key. A free Gemini key is never moved to a model that needs a paid key.
harness.fallbackIntro: What happens when an agent still fails after all its tries.
harness.fallback.offHint: The run stops. You can use Retry yourself.
harness.fallback.suggestHint: The run stops, and the Retry menu marks the model it suggests.
harness.fallback.autoHint: One more try with another model of the same provider. The cost cap still applies.

harness.retriesIntro: What happens when the provider is busy or a call fails for a reason that may pass (429, 500, 502, 503, 529, a network error). Other errors, such as a wrong key, are never retried.

harness.limit.retries.hint: 0 means a failed call stops the agent at once. 0 to 3.
harness.limit.retryDelay.label: Wait before each try
harness.retriesNote: Every try counts as a step, and the total time of 270 seconds still applies.
harness.costIntro: A run stops when its estimated cost passes this amount. Only agents on a paid key count; agents on a free Gemini key cost nothing. The estimate uses the prices in the catalog, so it can be a little off.
harness.limit.cost.label: Stop a run above
harness.costNote: Default: off. The cost is added up after each answer, so a run can go a little over before it stops.
harness.repeatIntro: Stops a run when the same agent gives the same answer again and again, which usually means it is stuck in a loop. Two answers count as the same when they match word for word, ignoring capital letters and spacing. It matters most for a supervisor and for debates.
harness.limit.repeat.label: Stop after the same answer
harness.limit.repeat.hint: Off, or 2 to 4 times in a row.
harness.repeatNote: Default: 3. A run stopped this way is saved, and the replay shows which agent repeated itself.
harness.handoffIntro: The most characters that one agent passes on to the next. A longer answer is cut and the next agent is told that it was cut. Your replay still shows the whole answer. This keeps long chains cheap.
harness.limit.handoff.label: Cut a handoff above
harness.handoffNote: Default: off. About 4 characters make one token, so 8,000 characters is roughly 2,000 tokens.

create.patternHelp: The orchestration pattern decides how the agents work together: who works when and who sees what. It also decides which connections the diagram allows. Changing it clears the diagram.

create.pattern.parallel: Several work at the same time, one combines the results, and more agents may follow to review or polish.

create.pattern.mapreduce: A splitter cuts the task into parts, one worker does each part at the same time, a reducer merges the results.
create.pattern.planexec: A planner writes a plan of steps once, an executor carries out the steps one after another.
agent.splitter.label: Splitter
agent.splitter.help: Cuts the task into two to six independent parts. It does not do the work itself.
agent.worker.label: Worker
agent.worker.help: Does one part of the task. It runs once for every part, all at the same time, and does not see the other parts.
agent.reducer.label: Reducer
agent.reducer.help: Merges the results of all the workers into one answer.
agent.executor.label: Executor
agent.executor.help: Carries out one step of the plan. It runs once for every step, one after another, and sees the results of the earlier steps.

tag.desc.handoff: One agent passes the work to another and the rest of the task goes on from there.
tag.desc.parallel-work: Several agents work on the same task at the same time, without seeing each other.
tag.desc.combining-answers: Several answers are merged into one, by a combiner or by a vote.
tag.desc.supervisor: A supervisor decides which worker goes next and when the work is done.
tag.desc.tool-choice: The agent chooses which tool to use, or whether to use one at all.
tag.desc.debate: Agents argue opposite sides and a judge reads the debate.
tag.desc.disagreement: The agents do not agree, and the run shows what happens then.
tag.desc.explaining: The task is to explain something clearly to a reader.
tag.desc.planning: The task is to make a plan, or to carry one out step by step.

tag.desc.risk-analysis: The task is to find what could go wrong and how bad it would be.
tag.desc.speed: The run shows what makes it faster or slower.
tag.desc.cost: The run shows what makes it cheaper or more expensive.

diagram.hover.state.waiting: It has not started yet. It starts when its turn comes.
diagram.hover.state.unreached: The run ended before it was reached.
diagram.hover.state.stopped: It was stopped before it finished.
diagram.hover.state.working: It is working now: the app is waiting for the model's reply.
diagram.hover.state.done: It is done and its answer is saved.
diagram.hover.state.error: It failed. Click it to see why.
diagram.hover.click: Click to see what it did.
diagram.hover.arrow.pending: Nothing has gone this way yet. The answer of {from} goes to {to} when {from} is done.
diagram.hover.arrow.used: The answer of {from} has gone to {to}.
diagram.hover.arrow.lit: The answer of {from} is going to {to} right now.
diagram.hover.badge.round: A debate runs in rounds. In each round every debater answers once and reads the answers of the others. After the last round the judge gives the verdict.
diagram.hover.badge.verdict: The rounds are over. The judge has read the whole debate and gives the verdict.
diagram.hover.badge.votes: Every voter answered on its own. The answer most of them agree on wins.
diagram.hover.badge.routed: The router read the task and chose this specialist. The others do not run.
diagram.hover.badge.handoff: Agents pass the task to each other. This is the agent that holds it now and how many times it has been handed over.
diagram.hover.badge.loop: A draft is judged and, if it is not good enough, sent back with feedback. This is the round the loop is in.
diagram.hover.badge.parts: The task was cut into parts that are worked on at the same time. This is how many.
diagram.hover.badge.steps: The plan has several steps that run one after another. This is the step that is running.
diagram.hover.typeChip: The pattern of this run: how its agents work together.
diagram.hover.recorded: The provider that answered when this run was made. Replaying it does not call the provider again.
diagram.hover.debate.judge.waiting: It takes no part in the rounds. It gets every argument, but reads them only after the last round, all at once, and then gives the verdict.
diagram.hover.debate.judge.working: The rounds are over. It is reading the whole debate and writing the verdict, which is the answer of the run.
diagram.hover.debate.judge.done: It has read the whole debate and given the verdict, which is the answer of the run.
diagram.hover.debate.judge.other: It takes no part in the rounds. After the last round it reads the whole debate once and gives the verdict.
diagram.hover.debate.debater.waiting: It is waiting for its turn. The debaters argue one after another, and each reads the whole debate so far.
diagram.hover.debate.debater.working: It is arguing now. It has read the whole debate so far, not only the last argument.
diagram.hover.debate.debater.done: It has argued in this round. It argues again in the next round, if there is one.
diagram.hover.debate.debater.other: The debaters argue one after another, and each reads the whole debate so far.
diagram.hover.debate.toJudge.pending: Nothing has gone this way yet. Every argument of {from} is sent to {to}, which only keeps them until the debate is over.
diagram.hover.debate.toJudge.used: Arguments of {from} have been sent to {to}. It does not answer them: it reads the whole debate once, after the last round.
diagram.hover.debate.toJudge.lit: An argument of {from} is going to {to} right now. It does not answer it: it reads the whole debate after the last round.
diagram.hover.debate.turn: {to} argues after {from} and reads the whole debate so far, not only the argument of {from}.
